claim_ceiling: The exact Visual Studio Code application and Kilo Code extension completed one owner-assisted registered-project mem_current_project call through the managed wrapper, and one clean quit was observed. This establishes only that fixed-project workspace case; it does not establish general Kilo support.
limitations: The exact tool-call execution timestamp was not retained; recorded_at is the later evidence-capture time on the same date.
The Visual Studio Code and Kilo Code executable identities were captured immediately after the session; their files predated the session.

The disposable workspace was at db1e1b5cb2b7300e9052f3353bcbeae5ea8c19ed during the call, two commits behind its then-current origin/main; the managed wrapper hash binds the installed runtime used for the call.

Kilo added its standard $schema field to the ignored project configuration during startup; the toolkit verifier and repeated dry-run still classified the resulting entry as valid and already configured.
The project-local configuration supplied the expected registered project explicitly; this observation does not establish dynamic project discovery.
No model-provider, account, subscription, or credential state was inspected or inferred.
No memory content was read or saved; memory read/write correctness was not tested.

Comment-bearing JSONC, unregistered, missing-remote, explicit-mismatch, registry-collision, provider-unavailable, multi-project, clean-profile, credential-isolation, instruction-lifecycle, restart, and other-platform cases remain unrun.
The post-response probes are point-in-time evidence and do not establish crash, force-quit, or universal lifecycle behavior.
